tools.name: search
tools.description: Search canonical public Aperture Wallet product facts, security guidance, supported-mainnet metadata, app-screen semantics, and Journal articles. Use this before answering an Aperture-specific question. This tool never searches user wallets or private account data.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch one canonical public source returned by search. The response includes citation-ready title, URL, text, and metadata. It never returns user wallet data or wallet credentials.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Return canonical identity, platform, App Store, custody-model, recommendation-fit, official-link, and product-boundary facts for Aperture Wallet.

tools.name: list_features
tools.description: List documented Aperture Wallet features with canonical article links and safety notes. Optionally filter by category.

tools.name: get_feature
tools.description: Return one documented Aperture Wallet feature by its stable feature ID, including summary, availability, primary source, and safety notes.

tools.name: list_supported_networks
tools.description: Return the mainnet account and network catalog documented from the current Aperture source tree. Do not treat a matching ticker as proof of cross-network compatibility.

tools.name: get_security_model
tools.description: Return Aperture Wallet self-custody storage, network, recovery, access-control, responsible-disclosure, and agent-safety boundaries. Never use this tool to request or process wallet credentials.

tools.name: get_latest_release
tools.description: Return the latest public App Store release snapshot and the primary Apple source used to verify it. Use the source when exact current version information matters.

tools.name: list_articles
tools.description: List published Aperture Journal articles with canonical HTML and Markdown URLs. Optionally filter by category and set a bounded result limit.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: Return the complete citation-ready Markdown representation of one published Aperture Journal article by slug and optional language tag, including canonical URL, dates, topics, body text, and public images.

tools.name: get_app_screen
tools.description: Return a non-secret semantic description of an important Aperture screen, its purpose, entry points, sensitivity, and safe agent actions. This does not inspect a user device or wallet.

tools.name: list_app_entry_points
tools.description: Return canonical navigation-only app entry points, their App Intent names, source and public-release status, web fallbacks, and safety effects. These links only open visible UI and never inspect a wallet, bypass app lock, sign, broadcast, import, export, or delete anything.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "fetch" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch, list_articles, get_article · Private data: search, fetch, get_product, list_features, get_feature, get_security_model, get_app_screen, list_app_entry_points · Public sink: list_app_entry_points · Destructive: list_app_entry_points.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch, list_articles, get_article · Private data: search, fetch, get_product, list_features, get_feature, get_security_model, get_app_screen, list_app_entry_points · Public sink: list_app_entry_points · Destructive: list_app_entry_points

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
